# ADO405: continue-on-error

continueOnError: true hides failures.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Category** | Best practices |
| **Default severity** | info |
| **Enabled by default** | no (enable with `--enable ADO405` or in `.adolint.yaml`) |
| **Checked on** | the template-expanded pipeline (positions point at the original files) |

## Description

A step or job with continueOnError: true doesn't fail the run when it fails. The run is reported as partially succeeded. Off by default because it is usually deliberate (cache restores, optional uploads); enable it to audit them.

## Example

Problem:

```yaml
- script: ./run-tests.sh
  continueOnError: true
```

Instead:

```yaml
- script: ./run-tests.sh
```

## Configuration

Change the severity or turn the rule off in `.adolint.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  ADO405: info   # off | info | warning | error
```

Or on the command line: `adolint lint --disable ADO405` or `--enable ADO405`.

Suppress a single finding with a comment on the line before it (or `disable-line` at the end of the line):

```yaml
# adolint:disable-next-line ADO405
```
